Search terms for this lesson“how do I climb a ladder?”Outline only

Short lesson (~15 min) + Cave Level Studio. Your PlayerController.Update() already switches between top-down movement (if (!isPlatformer)) and gravity-driven platforming (else). Today you reuse that single boolean: touching a "Ladder" trigger sets isPlatformer = false, and leaving sets isPlatformer = true. Then spend the rest of class building out your cave level for the boss fight.

Break It Down~10 minOutline only

Let the player climb ladders up and down without writing a second movement controller.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Mark every ladder object with a Ladder trigger colliderwhat does this part do?Read: 2.1 (creating and assigning tags, plus Collider2D Is Trigger)
  2. Switch out of platformer mode on trigger enterwhat does this part do?Read: PlayerController.OnTriggerEnter2D() (CompareTag("Ladder") -> isPlatformer = false; and rb.gravityScale = 0;)
  3. Restore platformer mode on trigger exitwhat does this part do?Read: PlayerController.OnTriggerExit2D() (CompareTag("Ladder") -> isPlatformer = true; and rb.gravityScale = gravityScale;)

Look at PlayerController.Update(): you ALREADY wrote if (!isPlatformer) { rb.linearVelocity = new Vector2(xVector, yVector); }. When you touch a ladder, you already have a mode switch that turns vertical W/S input on — all a ladder needs is flipping isPlatformer and zeroing gravity while overlapping the trigger.

Your turn

Pick two of the parts above and say in one line what each one actually does.

Look at PlayerController.Update(): why does setting isPlatformer = false; make vertical climbing (W/S or Up/Down arrows) work immediately without writing any new rb.linearVelocity line?

In addition to setting isPlatformer = false;, why is it helpful to set rb.gravityScale = 0; on trigger enter and restore rb.gravityScale = gravityScale; on exit?

If your ladder is solid instead of marked Is Trigger, which callback fires instead — and why would the player fail to walk onto the ladder?

In the Editor: Set Up the Ladder Trigger (~5 min) ~5 min
  1. Open Assets/Scenes/Platformer.unity and select Tag Manager (Inspector → Tag → Add Tag...) to add a tag named Ladder (exact spelling).
  2. Place your ladder sprite/GameObject in the cave, tag it Ladder, attach a BoxCollider2D, and check Is Trigger.
  3. Adjust Sorting Layer / Order in Layer so the player draws in front of the ladder rungs while climbing.
In the Code: Toggle isPlatformer in Trigger Callbacks (~10 min) ~10 min

Open Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs. You already have OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other) and OnTriggerExit2D(Collider2D other):

CallbackConditionWhat to set inside the branch
OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other) other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ladder") isPlatformer = false; and rb.gravityScale = 0;
OnTriggerExit2D(Collider2D other) other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ladder") isPlatformer = true; and rb.gravityScale = gravityScale;
Why zero rb.gravityScale only for ladders? Notice we stored [SerializeField] float gravityScale; in 6.1 instead of hardcoding a constant. When exiting a ladder trigger, setting rb.gravityScale = gravityScale; returns the exact weight you tuned in the Inspector.

Socratic: Reusing State

  1. In PlayerController.Update(), pressing KeyCode.J only fires inside the else branch of if (!isPlatformer). Does jumping work while climbing, and is that what your cave wants?
  2. What happens if you climb past the top of the ladder trigger box while still holding Up — which callback runs the frame your collider leaves the trigger?
  3. Why does checking other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ladder") keep coins, enemy swings, and fireballs from accidentally putting the player into climbing mode?
  4. What would break if you hardcoded rb.gravityScale = 1; on exit when your Player prefab expects gravityScale = 4.5?
Studio Time: Build Out Your Cave Level (~50 min) ~50 min

With ladders working, spend the rest of class shaping Platformer.unity toward the upcoming boss fight:

  • Connect lower and upper shafts using a mix of ladders, moving platforms (6.3), and tagged Ground jumps.
  • Place TurretController hazards and patrolling EnemyController enemies to guard shortcuts or coins.
  • Test the entire cave from Start (index 0) → Overworld → Platformer so every room flows toward where your boss door will sit.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Enter a "Ladder" trigger and climb up/down smoothly using isPlatformer = false
  • Exit the ladder trigger back into normal gravity and platforming (isPlatformer = true)
  • Build out multi-level shafts in your cave combining ladders, moving platforms, and enemies
  • Commit and push
